title: Price sensitivity + headcount jump probability bridge (Sept 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Small working memo to capture a compact model that bridges pricing sensitivity to a headcount jump (hiring + contractors) and the probability weighting across scenarios. Intended as a lightweight input to tpl-budgets v3 and the exec ask for a 30% runway cushion. Keep it pragmatic: triggers -> needed hires -> cost -> net margin impact.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline: current token price mix (hosted API + Dedicated) yields a projected gross margin of 48% in FY27E under current pricing and HC plan.
- Shock scenarios: a sustained 20% price compression (market reaction) causes revenue per token to drop -> requires either 18% headcount reduction or a targeted hiring freeze + 14% efficiency via Optimize features (quantization, caching) to hold margin targets.
- Bridge model output: present expected value of three actionable options (soft hiring pause, targeted automation investment, price-flooring for enterprise) with estimated probability-weighted runway improvements.

Key assumptions (callouts):
- Token mix: 65% generation (latency-sensitive), 25% embeddings, 10% reranking.
- Average revenue per 1M tokens baseline: $1,200 (mix-weighted).
- Cost-of-serving per 1M tokens baseline: $620.
- Typical hire (infra/ops or infra-engineer) fully-loaded cost: $240k/year (salary+burden+tools). Contractor day-rate converted to FTE at 0.2 of a headcount for short-burst work.
- Ramp: new hires assumed 60% productivity in q1 after hire, 85% in q2 onwards.

Scenario table (text matrix):
- Scenario A (Base): price stable, no incremental hires beyond plan. P=0.55.
  - HC plan: +12 net FTEs across infra/serving/observability in FY27.
  - Impact: margin +1.5 pts vs current forecast.
- Scenario B (Price compression -20% sustaining): P=0.25.
  - Options: (B1) hiring pause + Optimize uptake (capex $1.2M) or (B2) selective firing (-15% HC) or (B3) price floor for dedicated customers (negotiation).
  - Estimated cost to restore margin: B1 $1.2M CAPEX + 0.6M ops savings Y1; B2 labor savings $3.6M Y1; B3 revenue uplift uncertain (neg P&L timing lag).
- Scenario C (Demand spike +40% tokens): P=0.20.
  - Need: burst capacity (spot + short-term contractors) equivalent to 22 FTEs for 12 weeks; expected revenue > incremental cost -> margin accretive if priced correctly.

Probability bridge methodology (short):
- Map external signals to scenario probs: public competitor price cuts, new open model release, enterprise contract churn signals.
- Use binary trigger flags: competitor_drop_>10pct (sliding 30d window), commit_loss_top10_customers, model-mix-shift-index. Each flag adjusts scenario probs by +/–0.08.

Headcount jump mapping (when to hire vs contractor):
- Triggered hires (permanent) when demand signal sustained >3 months AND projected utilization >85% for Dedicated pool.
- Contractors used for 8–14 week bursts when signal is transient or when lead-time to hire >10 weeks.
- Example mapping: 1 sustained +10% token demand over baseline => 4 contractors for 10 weeks (equiv. 0.77 FTE-year) OR 1 perm hire with ramp cost.

Sample micro-sensitivity output (single-sheet style text):
- Inputs: price_delta_pct, token_change_pct, optimize_savings_pct, hires_planned (#).
- Outputs: delta_revenue, delta_cost (compute + labor), net_margin_delta, runway_delta_weeks.

Example runs (rounded):
1) price_delta -20%, token change 0%, optimize_savings 12% (capex $1.2M)
   - delta_revenue: -$6.0M/year, delta_compute_cost: -$1.1M (less tokens), net_margin_delta: -$5.1M -> to offset we need either $5.1M labor savings (~21 FTEs) or $1.2M capex + operational adjustments (eat remaining $3.1M via discounts/commits).
2) token +40%, price stable, hires planned +18 FTEs (mix infra/ops): incremental revenue $9.6M, incremental cost $4.3M -> net +$5.3M, runway +6 weeks.

Triggers & playbook (operational checklist):
- Monitor daily: price-change index (competitor public APIs), top-50 customer usage delta, Dedicated pool utilization (15 min aggregation).
- If competitor_drop_>10pct for 7 days: escalate to pricing@ and growth@; run quick EV calc; set temp hold on net-new hires for 2 weeks pending deeper review.
- If commit_loss_top5_customers projected >$200k MRR: immediate leadership review; consider targeted retention credits vs price-floor negotiation.
- If Dedicated utilization >92% for 14 days: approve 30-day contractor burst immediately; open reqs for permanent hires (priority infra-serving).

Open questions (for modeling team):
- Verify compute cost step function at scale (we used linearized cost per 1M tokens; need per-model kernel mix adjustments).
- Build quick Monte Carlo harness to sample the three scenarios and produce probability-weighted runway outcomes (ask: data-science help, ticket FIN-489).

Next steps / owner action items:
- Finance: wire in this compact bridge into tpl-budgets v3 inputs (owner: Maya) by 2026-09-15.
- Infra/Product: validate optimize_savings estimates and capex sizing (owner: Priya) by 2026-09-12.
- Sales/Account execs: surface price-floor levers and negotiated commit language options (owner: Diego) by 2026-09-20.

Notes to self (informal):
- This is intentionally rough; prefer an actionable trigger/playbook over perfect accuracy.
- Save detailed tables to the sheet prototype: /sheets/FIN/prototype/price-hc-bridge-2026 (placeholder).

References: CONFLUENCE:FIN-ops/price-sensitivity-playbook, JIRA:FIN-482 (modeling request), GH PR: redwood/ops-budget#314 (cost mapping).
